I5.quote: Hydrogen spillover (H-spillover) is the surface migration of activated hydrogen atoms from a metallic particle, on which they are generated, onto a support.
I5.location: main, p. 2, Abstract (first sentence of the article after the HAL cover page)

notes: Experimental plus DFT study of H-spillover on Pd-doped oxidized CNTs, so not theoretical_only. H-spillover is probed by the WO3 colour test quantified by UV-Vis DRS (Table 1 '%spillover', normalised 0-100%, main p. 14; Figure 4, p. 17), TPD-MS after H2 treatment ('TPD-MS was finally performed to quantify the amounts of H2, H2O, CO, and CO2 released', main p. 12; Figure 2c in normalized intensity), and NAP-XPS at 1 mbar H2 (main p. 19). None is a gravimetric, volumetric or flow uptake value; TPD alone does not meet I1 (Amendment 1). Exclusion therefore no_conditions_stated (I1 failure, not computational-only, not electrochemical). Only the main-text PDF (HAL accepted manuscript, 41 pages) was in the input; the SI was not supplied, but its listed contents (main p. 30) name no H2 uptake isotherm or capacity measurement. For information only: surface areas are reported (CNT 220 m2 g-1, p. 9; Pd/CNT 232 m2 g-1, p. 10), so I4 would be met if assessed. not_primary, retracted and duplicate_data do not apply (research article; is_retracted false; no statement of prior publication).
